ch38.df.d.part: Particle sent one at a time through the structure to the screen
ch38.df.d.v: Speed $v$ of the particle (log scale); momentum $p = \gamma m v$
ch38.df.d.st: Periodic structure the particles pass (auto: the classic experiment for each particle)
ch38.df.goal.dots: Each particle lands at a single point, yet many of them build an interference pattern: matter has a wave nature
ch38.df.goal.scale: Fringes show only when the wavelength $\lambda = h/p$ is not tiny compared with the spacing $d$ (fringe spacing $\Delta y \approx \lambda L/d$)
ch38.df.obs.single: One dot = one particle. Where a single particle lands cannot be predicted; only its probability distribution $\lvert\psi\rvert^2$ (dashed) is fixed
ch38.df.obs.dg: 54 eV electrons ($4.36\times10^6$ m/s) on nickel: $\lambda$ = 0.167 nm, first order at 51° (Davisson-Germer 1927 measured 50°)
ch38.df.obs.speed: Faster electrons: shorter wavelength, smaller angles, higher orders appear. Below 32.5 eV ($3.38\times10^6$ m/s) $\lambda > d$: no first order
ch38.df.obs.neutron: Thermal neutrons at 2200 m/s: $\lambda$ = 0.180 nm, first order at 57° on nickel; neutron diffraction is used to determine crystal structures
ch38.df.obs.c60: C₆₀ at 220 m/s on a 100 nm grating: $\lambda$ = 2.5 pm (1/400 of the 1 nm molecule), fringe spacing 31 μm at 1.25 m (Arndt et al. 1999)
ch38.df.obs.ball: Baseball at 40 m/s: $\lambda = 1.1\times10^{-34}$ m, $\Delta y \approx 10^{-31}$ m behind the 1 mm slit pair: only the two shadows of the slits, no wave behaviour can be seen
ch38.df.obs.same: Electrons or C₆₀ sent through the 1 mm slit pair (Structure in the settings) also give just two shadows: what decides is $\lambda/d$, not the kind of particle
ch38.df.as.model: Screen distribution: the Fraunhofer intensity $\lvert\psi\rvert^2$ (interference of $N$ periods × envelope of the opening $a$ × obliquity $\cos^2\theta$), shifted over the slit positions and widths. It tends to the Fraunhofer pattern when the fringes are large and to the geometric shadow of the slits when they are tiny
ch38.df.as.struct: Crystal: nickel surface-row spacing 0.215 nm, 20 point scatterers, screen 5 cm behind (simplified to transmission). Grating: period 100 nm, slit width 50 nm, 20 periods, screen 1.25 m behind. Double slit: spacing 1 mm, width 0.25 mm, screen 1 m behind
ch38.df.as.res: Fringe resolution criterion $\delta$ = 1/96 of the screen height (two histogram bins). For $\Delta y < \delta$ the central and first-order fringes form one block in the histogram: the fringes count as unresolved and the $\Delta y$ marker is hidden (numbers in the Σ panel)
ch38.df.as.size: Particle size ignored: particles larger than the structure (C₆₀ in a crystal, a baseball at 1 mm slits) are assumed to pass
ch38.df.as.beam: Single speed and a parallel incident beam. In real experiments the speed spread and beam divergence blur the fringes
ch38.df.as.rel: Relativistic momentum $p = \gamma m v$ ($\gamma$ = 1.15 for the fastest electrons, $1.5\times10^8$ m/s)
ch38.df.as.anim: Apparatus and flying dots not to scale (only the double slit shares the screen's scale). Stops at 3000 hits
